units.name: Debt scoring model
units.summary: Pure, I/O-free functions turn quiz evidence, centrality, churn and commit decay into per-unit understanding, debt and a 0-100 debt index, plus team bus-factor view.
units.decision: Importance = 0.6*centrality/5 + 0.4*churn; evidence is 1/0.5/0/-0.5 (confident wrong); verified = clamped mean of last K records; understanding decays 0.9 per later commit touching the unit; debt = importance*(1-understanding); team understanding = max over developers.
units.alternatives: Provenance-based scoring; time-based decay; static-analysis importance; team understanding as mean rather than max; ML-calibrated scores.
units.why: BRIEFING: provenance misstates architectural understanding; confident misconceptions should cost more than gaps; commit decay makes debt grow while AI builds. Pure functions keep it testable.

units.name: LLM backend via claude CLI
units.summary: An LLM protocol (structured/text) implemented by ClaudeCLI, which shells out to `claude -p` with read-only tools and JSON schema, and by a deterministic FakeLLM selected with UDEBT_LLM=fake.
units.decision: Call the local `claude` CLI as a subprocess (subscription-billed, tools limited to Read/Glob/Grep, structured output via --json-schema), with a prompt-marker-keyed FakeLLM for offline tests.
units.alternatives: Anthropic API SDK with an API key; other providers; local models; mocking per-test with unittest.mock.
units.why: No API key or runtime dependency needed (stdlib only), the model can explore the repo itself with read tools, and fake mode enables end-to-end CLI tests.

units.name: Prompts and JSON schemas with TASK markers
units.summary: Prompt builders and JSON schemas for map, questions, grade and dig; each prompt begins with a TASK: marker that FakeLLM dispatches on.
units.decision: Contract with the LLM is a JSON schema plus a prompt starting with a `TASK:` marker; FakeLLM parses the prompt text (e.g. '- unit_id:' lines, 'ANSWER:' lines) to produce canned answers.
units.alternatives: Separate method per task on the LLM interface; templating files; free-form text parsing.
units.why: Keeps one generic structured() entry point while letting the fake emulate each task; unclear beyond testing convenience.

units.name: JSON files under .udebt/, committed
units.summary: All state lives in .udebt/: shared map.json, per-developer append-only records/<email-slug>.jsonl, and optional config.json.
units.decision: Plain JSON/JSONL files in the repo, one record file per developer (keyed by git email slug), append-only; config loaded fresh with defaults.
units.alternatives: SQLite; a hosted service; storing in git notes; an untracked local cache.
units.why: Zero dependencies, diff-friendly, and per-developer files avoid merge conflicts while enabling team view via git.

units.name: Git helpers and developer identity
units.summary: Thin subprocess wrappers around git for repo root, HEAD, user identity, tracked files and commit counts touching paths since a given commit.
units.decision: Shell out to git; identify developers by git config user.email slug; commit churn per unit's paths drives both importance and decay; if the recorded head is gone (rebase) fall back to counting all commits.
units.alternatives: GitPython/libgit2; explicit user accounts; file-content hashing for change detection.
units.why: Stdlib-only constraint and commit-count is a cheap proxy for change; identity from git needs no auth.

units.name: Architectural map generation
units.summary: `udebt map` sends tracked files to the LLM, receives units, then attaches unique ids, churn, importance and preserved scope before saving map.json.
units.decision: The LLM proposes architectural units (decisions/modules/boundaries/flows), the code adds churn and importance, and previously set blackbox scopes survive regeneration by id.
units.alternatives: File- or directory-level units; static analysis/import graph; hand-authored maps.
units.why: BRIEFING: measure understanding of architecture, not files; package internals are out of scope; blackbox is a deliberate-ignorance declaration.

units.name: Prediction quiz and grading flow
units.summary: Pick highest-debt units, LLM generates questions, developer answers with confidence, LLM grades against code, results are appended as records and status is shown.
units.decision: Measure understanding by prediction questions graded by an LLM against the code; blank answers are 'unknown' with no penalty; confidence >=3 with wrong answer is a misconception.
units.alternatives: Multiple-choice quizzes; provenance tracking; self-reported understanding; deterministic grading.
units.why: BRIEFING: prediction tests the real mental model; known unknowns should not be penalized.

units.name: udebt CLI surface
units.summary: argparse commands (init, map, units, scope, quiz, status [--team], dig) with global --repo/--model/--as-user, orchestrating the other modules and formatting the debt tables.
units.decision: Single stdlib argparse entry point where cmd_* functions wire store, git, LLM and scoring; errors become SystemExit messages; --as-user overrides identity.
units.alternatives: Click/Typer; a library API or web UI; editor/hook integration (deferred).
units.why: Stdlib-only runtime and a team-oriented CLI product per BRIEFING.

units.name: Guided dig walkthrough
units.summary: `udebt dig` asks the LLM for a markdown walkthrough ending in 'CHECK QUESTION:', then optionally quizzes and records the answer.
units.decision: Free-text LLM output parsed with a regex for a trailing CHECK QUESTION line, reusing the grade/record path.
units.alternatives: Structured walkthrough output via schema; separate learning-record type.
units.why: Teaching text is easier as free-form markdown; reuses the quiz evidence pipeline so learning counts toward scores.
